pr_title: Set standard handles explicitly when starting a process with `-NoNewWindow`
pr_body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

## PR Summary

Fix #24986

This is a follow-up fix to the changes introduced by #20853.

- If we are starting a process with a new window, we should leave the standard handles unset when they are not redirected and let Windows figure out the default to use creating the process. Otherwise, the standard input of the new window will be tied with the old window for some reason and causes the new window to be unusable.
- If we are starting a process re-using the current window (with `-NoNewWindow`), then we need to explicitly set all the standard handles, especially when any of them is redirected. Otherwise, the un-redirected handles will become invalid.

issue_context.title: `Start-Process` in 7.5.0: invalid handles, no output emitted on Windows
issue_context.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] Write a descriptive title.
- [x] Make sure you are able to repro it on the [latest released version](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases)
- [x] Search the existing issues.
- [x] Refer to the [FAQ](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/master/docs/FAQ.md).
- [x] Refer to [Differences between Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/whats-new/differences-from-windows-powershell).

### Steps to reproduce

Run the following on Windows:

```powershell
Start-Process -Wait -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardError tmp.txt -FilePath cmd -ArgumentList "/C echo Hello"
```

### Expected behavior

```console
This should output `Hello` and produce an empty `tmp.txt` file.
```

### Actual behavior

```console
On Windows:
- There is no stdout output
- A `tmp.txt` file is produced, with the following content: `The handle is invalid.`

On WSL, everything works as expected, but the command needs to be adjusted:


Start-Process -Wait -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardError tmp.txt -FilePath bash -ArgumentList '-c "echo Hello"'
```

### Error details

```console
PowerShell does not return an error, `Get-Error` doesn't return anything.
```

### Environment data

```powershell
Name                           Value
----                           -----
PSVersion                      7.5.0
PSEdition                      Core
GitCommitId                    7.5.0
OS                             Microsoft Windows 10.0.22631
Platform                       Win32NT
PSCompatibleVersions           {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0…}
PSRemotingProtocolVersion      2.3
SerializationVersion           1.1.0.1
WSManStackVersion              3.0
```

### Visuals

7.5.0:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29ee5e34-fa9a-4172-b854-78fdc3ce8d5b)

5.1, but the same thing happens in 7.4:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/955fd139-c8d0-49f2-934d-a0f904062fe6)
comments: To be clear, given that "breaking change" could be misconstrued to have been intentional: we're clearly dealing with a (newly introduced) _bug_ here.
/cc @daxian-dbw Could you please comment the issue?

Confirmed in 7.5, 7.6. Not present in 7.4 and WPS. When you also -RedirectStandardOutput, the exception is not raised BTW:

` Start-Process -Wait -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardError tmp.txt -RedirectStandardOutput tmp2.txt -FilePath cmd -ArgumentList "/C echo Hello"; get-content .\tmp.txt, .\tmp2.txt`

It seems to misbehave when `-NoNewWindow` is specified. More specifically, when the new process is going to reuse the current terminal/console. I will investigate further the next week when I have more time.
